title: WaveNet: A generative model for raw audio
summary: Google DeepMind publicly presented WaveNet on September 8, 2016 as a deep generative model of raw audio waveforms. The associated research described WaveNet as a probabilistic autoregressive neural network that generates raw audio sample by sample and demonstrated applications including text-to-speech and music generation.
significance: A documented generative-audio research milestone for direct modeling of raw audio waveforms with an autoregressive neural network.

verification.note: Google DeepMind's first-party research post establishes September 8, 2016 as the public research-introduction date and directly supports the raw-audio generative-model and speech/music claims. The original WaveNet arXiv paper, first submitted September 12, 2016, independently supports the authorship, probabilistic autoregressive formulation, raw-waveform generation, text-to-speech, and music-generation claims. The event date is therefore attached specifically to the DeepMind public research introduction, not asserted as a software-release, API, deployment, or model-training completion date. No geography, ancestry, downstream influence, causality, or relationships are inferred.
